Definition: Nergal-Sharetser, the name of two Babylonians
BiblicalUsage: Nergal-sharezer is the name of two Babylonian princes, and both appear on the day Jerusalem falls: one sits in the middle gate with the other princes when the city is taken, and one is sent to fetch Jeremiah out of the prison court. The same name stands at the gate of judgment and at the door of the prophet's release.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God writes even the enemy's names into the story, because no prince of Babylon moves except on the edge of His purposes.
